The story is a cohesive and atmospheric character study where every element—setting, action, and dialogue—serves a unified theme. The mechanics of the reaction ferry, which relies entirely on a steel cable and the river's current to navigate through thick fog without sight, serve as a direct reflection of the protagonist, Ilse. Her stoic, grounded nature and reliance on routine are established through her brief, dry interactions with the three passengers. When the emotional climax occurs in the middle of the river—an unexpected phone call from an estranged figure named Jonas (likely her son)—her decision not to answer it ("Ich fahre" / "I am driving") is completely earned by the narrative setup. Just as the cable holds the ferry steady when neither shore is visible, her duty and routine anchor her through emotional uncertainty until the other side of the river finally emerges from the fog.
